briefs.problem: Freelancer missions can end without the right people being warned in time to act (renew, invoice, validate, offboard); the actual consequence has not been stated by the client.
briefs.solution: A scheduled, lead-time-based reminder on the Mission end date that notifies recipients chosen by contact role (and possibly an internal owner), reusing the platform's existing role-based notification routing where it fits.
introduces: a scheduled trigger on Mission end dates, distinct from the existing event-driven end-of-mission notifications

challenges.headline: Build before checking existing notifications
challenges.premise: A new notification capability needs to be built for mission end.
challenges.alternative: The platform already has role-based notifications, Contact roles and a Mission with an end date. A first version may be configuration or a thin scheduled job on top of that routing, rather than a new notification engine.
challenges.consequence: Building a parallel mechanism duplicates routing logic and creates a second place where recipient rules must be maintained, per client.
challenges.recommendation: Before estimating, check what the current notification feature can do today (including any reminder capability not switched on) and size only the gap: the scheduled lead-time trigger.

challenges.headline: A notice may not be enough
challenges.premise: Telling people the mission is about to end is the whole need.
challenges.alternative: If the real pain is missed renewals or late final invoicing, the notice should link to the action (extend the mission, prepare the final invoice) or be tied to a tracked follow-up. If the pain is only awareness, a plain reminder is sufficient and much cheaper.
challenges.consequence: Without knowing the intended action, we risk shipping a reminder that is ignored, or silently growing into a renewal and invoicing workflow.
challenges.recommendation: Get the client to name what goes wrong today when nobody is warned, and decide explicitly whether version one is alert-only.

challenges.headline: One lead time versus configurable rules
challenges.premise: 'About to end' and 'the right people' can be defined once, or per client.
challenges.alternative: A single global rule (for example one lead time and recipients by role) ships faster; per-client configuration needs a settings model and an admin screen. These figures are proposals, not client-stated values.
challenges.consequence: Starting with per-client configuration front-loads admin UI and testing, while starting global may force rework if clients differ, as this platform's routing often does.
challenges.recommendation: Ask whether clients genuinely differ; if unknown, start with a global default and a data model that can later be overridden per client.

challenges.headline: Alert versus follow-up process
challenges.premise: A notification is enough. The request treats 'notify the right people' as the whole job.
challenges.alternative: End of mission is already an event on this platform that can trigger final invoicing and validation. A reminder that links to the mission and names the next action (renew, invoice, close) would serve those follow-ups better than a bare alert. Whether the reminder must be acknowledged is a separate choice and can wait.
challenges.consequence: If the real need is renewal decisions or final invoicing, an informational email gets read and ignored. The team then adds acknowledgement, escalation and status tracking later, which is a different build.
challenges.recommendation: Before estimating, ask the client what each recipient should do after being warned. Build only the notification if the answer is 'just be aware'.

challenges.headline: Undefined 'right people'
challenges.premise: Recipients can be settled later or hardcoded. The request assumes a single obvious audience.
challenges.alternative: Define recipients by contact role (operational, billing) and by internal role. Propose a default recipient set that clients can override. This reuses the existing role model rather than adding a new one.
challenges.consequence: A hardcoded recipient list will be wrong for some clients. A client with no contact in the needed role means the warning silently goes nowhere. Freelancer and contact data also raises GDPR and visibility questions.
challenges.recommendation: Agree a recipient matrix with the client, including a fallback when no contact exists in the needed role.

challenges.headline: Build before checking reuse

challenges.alternative: If the platform already has role-based notification routing or a scheduler, this may be a configuration of an existing rule on the Mission end date rather than new code.
challenges.consequence: Building a parallel notification path duplicates routing logic and creates a second place to maintain recipients and templates.
challenges.recommendation: Audit existing notification and scheduling capabilities, and how end-of-mission is handled today, before committing to a build.

challenges.headline: Notify without a defined action
challenges.premise: Telling people that a mission is ending is the goal in itself.
challenges.alternative: Treat the reminder as the start of a follow-up (renew or extend, issue the final invoice, validate the mission). It can first be a plain heads-up that links to the mission, and repeat only while no decision is recorded.
challenges.consequence: A one-off alert that nobody has to act on is easily ignored, and the missed final invoices or validations that probably motivated the request would persist.
challenges.recommendation: Ask what happened on the last mission that ended unnoticed, and design the reminder around the follow-up it should have triggered.

challenges.headline: Build before checking existing notifications
challenges.premise: A new mission-end notification has to be built.
challenges.alternative: The platform already has role-based notifications and end-of-mission events. A scheduled trigger plugged into that routing may cover most of the need and avoid a separate mechanism.
challenges.consequence: A parallel notification path duplicates routing logic and creates a second place to maintain recipients and permissions.
challenges.recommendation: Review the current notification setup and how missions are tracked today before estimating, and reuse whatever routing exists.

challenges.headline: Assuming every mission has a reliable end date
challenges.premise: The mission end date is always present and current, so a time-based trigger will fire correctly.
challenges.alternative: Measure how many missions lack an end date or have a stale one, and decide on a rule (block creation without a date, or flag the gap) before relying on it as the trigger.
challenges.consequence: Missing or outdated dates mean silent non-warnings, or reminders for missions already extended, which erodes trust in the feature.
challenges.recommendation: Check end-date completeness on current missions, and define the behaviour for extensions and date edits.

decisions.decision: Treat this as an internal feature of the existing platform, with no separate payer or launch question
Use a scheduled, time-based trigger on the mission end date, separate from the end-of-mission event
decisions.why: 'About to end' means before the end date, so it cannot be driven by the end-of-mission event alone.
decisions.alternative: Notify only when the mission ends.
decisions.tradeoff: Adds a scheduler and duplicate handling, in exchange for warning people early enough to act.
